key_insight: A pathology foundation model combined with multiple instance learning graded Barrett’s esophagus dysplasia across institutions without stain normalization, achieving a macro-averaged AUC of 0.96.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more consistent dysplasia grading, where pathologist disagreement can complicate clinical decisions.
method: Retrospective study of 969 H&E-stained whole-slide images from four institutions.
Patch-level classifiers trained on expert annotations identified diagnostically relevant regions.
Attribute-aware multiple instance learning classified slides as non-dysplastic Barrett’s esophagus, low-grade dysplasia, or high-grade dysplasia.
evidence_signal: On 130 held-out slides, macro-averaged AUC was 0.96 (95% CI 0.93–0.98); binary dysplasia detection achieved 98% sensitivity and 81% specificity, with no high-grade case classified as non-dysplastic.
watch_item: Prospective validation in additional institutions and clinical workflows is needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
